source.title: No Spurious Local Minima: on the Optimization Landscapes of Wide and Deep Neural Networks

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper, though its title differs from the provided title: it is headed “Optimization Landscapes of Wide Deep Neural Networks Are Benign.”
record.tranche_reason: The paper gives theoretical results about optimization landscapes in wide neural networks, using absence of confined points and path connections rather than training-error experiments or gradient-descent measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theorems about confined points and global minima, not empirical runs or measured training classification error. The cited empirical and theoretical results in the introduction and discussion are prior work, not rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves landscape and global-minimizer existence results, but tests none of V1–V6. In particular, absence of confined points neither excludes suboptimal local minima nor establishes that gradient descent avoids them. It does not measure the teacher-student convergence behavior specified by V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors prove absence of confined points for sufficiently wide networks under their framework and argue that width makes optimization landscapes more benign. They acknowledge that the general sufficient width bound grows exponentially with depth and greatly exceeds practical widths. They also argue that unconstrained wide networks are problematic because almost every fixed inner-layer configuration permits a globally optimal output-layer completion. These are landscape and existence conclusions, without a convergence guarantee for a specified training algorithm.
record.recipe_differences: The paper provides theoretical landscape analysis rather than an empirical training recipe or benchmark evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: The stated width threshold depends exponentially on depth in the general theorem; for linear activation, the authors give a bound independent of depth. The paper also distinguishes constrained from unconstrained estimation.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 2 and 3 establish absence of confined points at their stated width bounds. Corollary 11 establishes path equivalence of all parameters under the general bound. Suboptimal local minima can still exist.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide feedforward networks in the stated framework admit nonincreasing paths from every parameter to a global minimum; the sufficient width bound is exponential in depth generally and independent of depth for linear activation.

fits_no_version.finding: For unconstrained networks with w ≥ 2m(n + 1), almost every fixed set of inner-layer parameters admits an output-layer completion attaining a global minimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Almost every fixed inner-layer configuration of sufficiently wide unconstrained networks can be completed to a global minimizer by choosing the output layer.

record.problems: The central result is theoretical and does not measure training-error outcomes or demonstrate that a gradient-based algorithm reaches a global minimum. The authors state that the general width bound grows exponentially with depth and is much wider than networks used in practice; whether the depth dependence can be improved generally remains open.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying result rows were left out. Cited empirical evidence and results from other papers were excluded.

untested.parts: SGD or Adam training from random initialization; near-zero classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels; effects of size, early stopping, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student gradient descent; frequencies of convergence to spurious minima; effects of adding one or two student neurons at widths 6–20.
Training-error degradation with depth, identity-shortcut comparisons, special initialization of plain tanh networks, and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization-dependent signal and gradient propagation, learning speed, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability trajectories, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The practical width limitation qualifies the study's own theorem, not any tested claim version. The state corrections concern the rows' inability to determine V1–V6; they do not dispute the recorded theorem statements.

versions.untested_parts: Training from random initialization, gradient-based optimization, and training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 or corrupted labels.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student gradient descent, spurious-minimum frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.
Comparisons of plain and residual networks by depth and training error; special initializations and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate regimes, loss trajectories, curvature or sharpness, and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons of training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: Wide feedforward networks in the Section 2.1 framework
rows.operation_detail: Theorem establishes absence of confined points in the empirical-risk objective over the stated network framework.

conditions.value: Elementwise; arbitrary function as specified in Section 2.1

rows.measure: Existence of confined points in the objective landscape
rows.value: The objective function has no confined points.
rows.note: This is a theoretical landscape result, not an observed training-error or gradient-descent result; no claim version directly names confined points.
rows.check: Theorem 2 is accurately recorded at w ≥ 2m(n + 1)^l, but its nonincreasing-path guarantee cannot establish any version's training behavior. This is a theoretical result, not an observed training outcome.

rows.subject: Wide feedforward networks with linear activation
rows.operation_detail: Theorem establishes absence of confined points in the empirical-risk objective for linear activation.
rows.measure: Existence of confined points in the objective landscape
rows.value: The objective function has no confined points.
rows.note: Theorem 3 removes the depth factor from the width bound for linear activation; it does not report training classification error.
rows.check: Theorem 3 is accurately recorded for linear activation at w ≥ 2m(n + 1). Its landscape guarantee does not measure gradient-descent outcomes, training speed, or trainable depth.

rows.subject: Unconstrained networks in the Section 2.1 framework
rows.operation_detail: Theorem establishes existence of an output-layer global minimizer for almost every fixed setting of inner-layer parameters.

conditions.value: Almost every choice of Θ^(l−1), …, Θ^0

rows.measure: Existence of a global minimum after fixing inner layers
rows.value: For Lebesgue-almost every fixed set of inner layers, there is a Θ^l making the full parameter a global minimum.
rows.note: This is a theoretical statement about global minima, not a measured training outcome.
rows.check: Theorem 4 states existence of an output-layer completion attaining a global minimum for almost every fixed set of inner layers. It establishes neither zero classification error nor convergence of a specified training algorithm.
